title: United States v. Avery R. Denslow
jurisdiction_basis: 18 U.S.C. § 3231; 28 U.S.C. § 1291; final judgment of conviction; offense alleged in San Francisco.

timeline.description: Fictional federal equipment award enters performance period.
Technician transfers two instruments to calibration vendor.
Property review sheet records six listed instruments; four are at facility, two at vendor.
Grant specialist requests clarification before deciding whether to close monitoring item.
Recorded interview in San Francisco includes charged answer.
Specialist receives vendor records and leaves item open.
Arraignment, not guilty plea, scheduling order.
Court enters reasoned ends-of-justice continuance to 2026-03-09.
Court enters reasoned ends-of-justice continuance to 2026-05-04.
Court enters reasoned ends-of-justice continuance to 2026-07-13.
Grant specialist and records witnesses testify.
Jury returns guilty verdict on count one.

facts.value: I checked all six before I signed.

issues.question: Whether the evidence at trial permitted a rational jury to find knowing and willful falsity of the charged answer and its materiality under 18 U.S.C. § 1001(a)(2).
issues.standard_of_review: De novo review of preserved Rule 29 sufficiency; evidence and reasonable inferences in government favor; not a credibility retrial.
issues.preservation_status: Preserved at close of government evidence and all evidence, renewed within 14 days after verdict.
issues.appellant_theory: The answer referred to reconciliation of records, not a representation of personally seeing every item; the wording and contemporaneous records do not exclude a reasonable understanding of a truthful answer. Actual decision process and ability to affect it must be evaluated.
issues.appellee_theory: Interview context, prior discussion and certification support a rational inference the speaker knowingly represented physical verification; answer could influence monitoring even if follow-up continued.
issues.appellant_relief: Reverse conviction and direct judgment of acquittal for insufficient evidence.
issues.ruling_quote: The renewed motion for judgment of acquittal is denied.
issues.preservation_quote: Defense renews the Rule 29 motion on falsity, knowledge and materiality.

brief_record_refs.quote: I have reviewed the attached property verification worksheet and associated records for the six listed instruments. To the best of my knowledge, the listed locations and custody information accurately reflect the property records reviewed. The basis of verification is identified on the worksheet; unresolved documentation is subject to follow-up.
brief_record_refs.review_status: Page anchor linked; merits and full-sentence review pending.

brief_record_refs.quote: The cooperative shall prepare a periodic property verification record for the award file. A physical check may be combined with reliable third-party custody records for equipment temporarily at a service vendor, provided that the basis of verification is identified accurately. The record should distinguish direct observation from documentary confirmation. The individual signing the verification record is responsible for reviewing the supporting material and identifying exceptions that require follow-up. The signature does not convert a vendor receipt into a personal observation. The agency may request additional records to clarify a location or verification method. A request for clarification is not, by itself, a finding that the item is missing. The agency specialist may close a monitoring item, request additional supporting records or refer an unresolved discrepancy for further review.
brief_record_refs.review_status: Page anchor linked; merits and full-sentence review pending.

brief_record_refs.quote: THE COURT: Counsel, are there other government witnesses today?
brief_record_refs.review_status: Page anchor linked; merits and full-sentence review pending.

brief_record_refs.quote: MR. CARROW: Defense renews the Rule 29 motion on falsity, knowledge and materiality. The testimony now confirms the review of the worksheet and transfer list. There is no dispute that the two instruments were at the vendor and that the defendant did not personally inspect them there before the signature. What is disputed is whether his answer represented that he did. The complete recording does not merely supply an after-the-fact excuse; it contains the clarification at the moment of the statement. The government must prove beyond a reasonable doubt both the false representation and that he knowingly and willfully made it. The actual monitoring process continued along the course already indicated by the April second email. The government has not established materiality of the charged words in their context.
